title: Guard the force-unwrapped credential.user in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.createUserWithEmailAndPassword
why: Every other credential.user access in this same file tolerates a null user (signInAndGetUser:74 and signInWithEmailLink:141 both route through _toAppUserOrNull). Here the `!` will throw a raw TypeError ('Null check operator used on a null value') instead of a typed, catchable error if Firebase ever returns a credential without a user — a TypeError carries no stable code (EH-5) and isn't a deliberately-thrown, meaningful exception, so it degrades straight to an opaque crash instead of a handleable condition, inconsistent with how the rest of the file treats the identical precondition.
recommendation: Mirror the null-check-and-throw pattern used elsewhere in the file (or the typed exception recommended in the EH-5 finding) instead of force-unwrapping credential.user.
acceptance_criteria: No bare `!` on credential.user in this file.
A regression test exercises the null-user branch of createUserWithEmailAndPassword.
